meta.title: Seasons Around the World — Set 5
meta.subject: English Reading
meta.description: Challenge quiz for 'Seasons Around the World' — inference, geography, and comparison.

questions.question: Why is it dark all day in winter near the North Pole?
options: Because there are too many storm clouds blocking the sun.
Because the Earth is tilted away from the sun, blocking its light.
Because the sun travels to the equator and stays there.
Because animals eat all the food under the ground.
questions.explanation: Because of Earth's tilt, the North Pole points completely away from the sun in winter, so it receives no sunlight at all.

questions.question: When it is winter in the northern part of the world (like Taiwan), it is summer in the southern part (like Australia).
questions.explanation: True. The two halves of the Earth always have opposite seasons because of how Earth tilts as it orbits the sun.

questions.question: Why does Antarctica never get warm, even in summer when the sun never sets?
options: Because the sun's rays hit it at a low angle, spreading out the heat.
Because the land is covered in dry sand.
Because it is located right on the equator.
Because the summer days are too short.
questions.explanation: At the poles, the sun is always low in the sky, so the sunlight is weak and spread out, keeping the temperature freezing.

questions.question: Near the equator, people experience four distinct seasons: spring, summer, autumn, and winter.
questions.explanation: False. Near the equator, the weather stays hot all year, so they only have wet and dry seasons, not four seasons.

questions.question: Why do some butterflies travel from the United States to Mexico in the fall?
options: To lay eggs on red oak trees.
To find a warmer climate so they can survive the winter.
Because Mexico is the coldest place on Earth.
To hibernate in deep caves.
questions.explanation: Butterflies are insects that cannot survive freezing temperatures, so they migrate to warmer Mexico for the winter.

questions.question: When it is winter in the northern part of the world, it is summer in the _______ part.
questions.hint: The half of the Earth opposite of northern.
questions.explanation: The Earth has two halves: the northern hemisphere and the southern hemisphere. They have opposite seasons.

questions.question: In fall, some trees drop their leaves. What does this help the trees do?
options: It helps them grow fruit.
It helps them save water and survive the cold winter.
It makes them grow new leaves immediately.
It keeps birds from building nests.
questions.explanation: Without leaves, trees do not lose as much water, which helps them survive during winter when water is frozen as ice.

questions.question: Sort these features based on whether they describe the North Pole or the Equator in winter:
questions.explanation: The North Pole in winter is completely dark with no sun. The equator has constant weather where seasons do not change.

questions.question: Some animals hibernate in winter to sleep through the months when food is hard to find.
questions.explanation: True. Hibernation is a way for animals to save energy and survive when there is very little food in winter.

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe the sun in Antarctica:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'The sun never sets in Antarctica.' This happens during their summer.

questions.question: Why do animals eat a lot in the fall?
options: Because they are growing taller.
To store fat and stay warm during winter when food is scarce.
Because they only like fall foods.
Because the rain makes them hungry.
questions.explanation: Eating a lot in fall helps animals build up body fat, which keeps them warm and provides energy when food is hard to find in winter.

questions.question: The coldest place on Earth is _______, where the sun never sets in summer.
questions.hint: The icy southern continent at the South Pole.
questions.explanation: Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth. Even in summer, it never gets warm.

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe the seasons near the equator:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Seasons don't change much near the equator.' The temperature stays hot.

questions.question: Plants stop growing or die in winter because there is less sunlight and liquid water is frozen.
questions.explanation: True. Plants need liquid water and sunlight to grow. In winter, water turns to ice and the days are shorter, so growth stops.

questions.question: How is spring near the equator different from spring in the northern part of the world?
options: It is much colder than summer near the equator.
It is very snowy like winter at the equator.
It has leaves changing colors and dropping.
It has no major weather change and is like all other seasons.
questions.explanation: In the north, spring brings warmth, rain, and new leaves. Near the equator, there is very little temperature change, so spring is like other seasons.
